messages:
Maria P.: Quick update — we’re launching A800S micro-pools in Santiago (SCL) and Jakarta (JKT) next week. :rocket:
Maria P.: Alongside the hardware rollout we’re introducing a new reservation mode called 'cold-reserve' (see brief below). This is aimed at improving overall utilization while preserving committed capacity when customers actually need it.
Arun K.: TL;DR on cold-reserve: if a reserved pool is idle for a configured window, eligible slots can be offered as transient burst capacity to other workloads. Reserved owner retains priority reclaim within reclaim_window.
Lena V.: Important operational notes: reclaim latency target is 10s for GPU handoff, but warm-up variations mean customers should set graceful timeouts. We’ll expose metrics in Console (reservations.metrics.cold_reserve.*).
Josh T.: Billing note: during cold-reserve usage, the reserved account pays the committed fee still, burst consumer pays transient usage at lower spot-like rate. Finance modeled expected uplift in utilization ~7-12% across impacted regions.
Sora L.: Support guidance: please reference KB link (coming) and use the pre-baked incident runbook when reclaim_fails. If customers object to any reclaim behavior we can override on a per-contract basis.
capacity-bot: Reminder — rollout plan: canary -> broader preview -> GA. Canary starts 2025-06-03 in SCL, 2025-06-04 in JKT.
Maria P.: Who needs early access for testing? Ping Arun or me. We’ll add teams to the canary project.
Arun K.: Ops checklist (short):
```
- Create micro-pool config: gpu_type=A800S, pool_size=8/16
- cold_reserve.window=3600  # seconds idle before offering
- reclaim_window=120       # seconds to reclaim for owner
- metrics.alert=on
```
Arun K.: We’ll schedule a small maintenance window to attach the pools to the control plane on the canary dates. Minimal impact expected.
Lena V.: SRE note: I’ll add e2e tests for reclaim flows and load tests for 95/99p handoff times.
Josh T.: Pricing update draft is in the finance doc — will share link in a follow-up. Key point: no change to committed pricing, a new transient burst SKU for cold-reserve consumers.
Sora L.: Prepping support FAQ and canned replies. If anyone has customer-facing language suggestions, drop them here.
Maria P.: A couple of customer-facing bullets to reuse:
- "Cold-reserve lets you get the utilization benefits of reserved pools while keeping predictable reclaimability for your commitments."
- "You keep priority access during your reclaim window; others can only use idle capacity transiently."
Arun K.: Ops policy change: admins can opt-out of cold-reserve per-reservation. Default is opt-in for new micro-pools. Existing reserved pools will NOT be auto opted-in; we’ll send targeted emails.
deploy-bot: Deployment scheduled: 2025-06-01 02:00 UTC — control plane changes for cold-reserve flags.
Maria P.: Action items:
- Arun: run canary ops and post canary playbook (before 2025-06-01)
- Lena: add reclaim e2e and perf dashboards
- Josh: finalize transient SKU pricing
- Sora: publish KB + support playbook
Maria P.: Thanks all — ping me for access to the canary project. :wave:
